ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC: 1927 The year 1927 will be the focal point for a wide-ranging seminar-style exploration of musical issues in America and Europe, including: the impact of technology (radio, recordings, film) on musical creation and dissemination, of machine aesthetics (pianolas, proto-electroacoustic experiments), of racial representations and assumptions, and of urbanization; the co-existing aesthetics of neoclassicism, serialism, neue Sachlichkeit, varieties of American modernism, Broadway, Tin Pan Alley, jazz, blues, the Harlem Renaissance, and their intersections. Readings, listening, and discussion will govern class meetings, culminating in a final research project that intersects meaningfully with the year 1927.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Restricted to Music or Musicology major(s).
